review_notes: The abstract and introduction define the central substantive question as whether discretionary-accrual boosting explains the earnings kink (physical pp. 1–3). The paper is not presented as a method paper: it tests the earnings-management explanation, and introduces the revised accrual proxy as one of four checks addressing the possibility that its proxy lacks power (p. 3).

Table 1 is a genuine fitted comparison, not just a borrowed calibration: the authors extend Jones and estimate four incremental accrual specifications across 637 two-digit-SIC/year groups, comparing mean coefficients and adjusted R² (pp. 4–8). The forward-looking variant is developed as a more explanatory DA construction. Under the frozen principal-question rule and scope clarification 01, however, these fits are indispensable measurement constructions supporting the substantive kink question, not its principal regression family.

The direct central tests are Table 3's comparisons of small-profit firms with all other firms and with small-loss firms (pp. 12–15). Table 3 reports differences in means and explicitly identifies its test statistics as t-tests (p. 14), so there is no eligible principal regression baseline to extract. Equations (3)–(4) construct DA inputs for those non-regression comparisons; under the frozen rule, construction fits cannot replace an absent baseline family or be retained as supporting models without one.

Table 2's earnings-component persistence regressions are introduced as a test validating the DA proxy's transitory component (p. 8; Table 2 pp. 10–11). The SEC enforcement and future-performance analyses are additional proxy-power checks (pp. 3, 8–9); Table 4 future-performance comparisons are also differences in means (pp. 13, 16). These validation/follow-up tests do not become the baseline for the central earnings-kink question. Thus the main empirical analysis contains no eligible baseline regression.
descriptive_reason: The frozen specification contains zero baseline models, so no baseline-linked descriptive group applies. Tables 3 and 4 are mean-comparison tests, and the other fitted tables are proxy construction, validation, or temporal trend analyses outside the principal baseline scope.
results_review_notes: The source-selected central tests compare small-profit firms with other firms and small-loss firms using sample mean differences in Tables 3 and 4; the Table 3 and Table 4 notes identify t-tests, not regression fits.

Tables 1 and 2 report accrual-proxy construction and validation regressions, while Table 5 is a secondary temporal trend analysis. None is the principal regression family for the earnings-management explanation under the frozen source-selection rule.
No baseline coefficients, standard errors, markers, fit statistics, or baseline descriptives are applicable to this paper.

calculation_provenance.policy: strict; no guessed degrees of freedom or normal approximations
